Focus on QPS/concurrency, token distribution (prompt/response), tail latency/p99, and whether Redwood Dedicated or VPC Private is required. Action items and timeline agreed; Redwood to provide harness and AzureGrove to share traces.
topics: Workload characterization (QPS, peak concurrency, diurnal patterns)
Token mix: input vs output distribution and typical prompt lengths

Benchmark plan: replay, synthetic tails, telemetry and metrics to collect
Deployment model: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC, data residency, encryption
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-11-19
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 62 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (AzureGrove Head of Platform), Lina Zhou (ML Eng), Omar Khalid (SRE)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey team thanks for carving out time. quick intro, im Jordan, ae on the account. Priya will run the technical piece. um carlos, do you want to kick off with context on what AzureGrove is trying to validate here?

[00:14] Carlos: Yeah thanks, Jordan. So uh short version: we run conversational product recs across web and mobile and we want to move from an API-first prototype into something that can handle production load. We're evaluating Redwood because of the cost/perf profile and the rollout options. main ask: can you prove you can hit our tail-latency and cost targets for a 1 month pilot then scale.

[00:33] Lina: i'll add, our traffic shape is weird — lots of low QPS long-tail bursts during flash sales. typical baseline QPS is around 120 qps global but we see spikes to about 1.8k qps for 10-20 minutes a few times per week. also prompt sizes vary - median input tokens ~45, median response ~120 but we have a 5% heavy-tail where responses go 600-1500 tokens.

[00:54] Omar: from infra side we need to check networking: we require VPC peering or private link for the POC if possible, and all logs must be pushed into our SIEM. also SOC2 is table stakes.

[01:12] Priya: thanks, that's helpful. so two immediate framing things: 1) workload characterization — qps, concurrency, and token distribution drive kernel selection, batching and caching behavior, and 2) success criteria — what p95/p99 latencies and cost per 1M tokens will you accept?

[01:34] Carlos: p99 under 350ms for single-turn gen would be ideal but we're willing to relax to 500ms if cost is reasonable. p95 under 180ms. Cost target we don't have a hard number yet but want a clear unit economics comparison vs our in-house infra.

[01:50] Jordan: ok good. quick question on model: are you using a single model family now or mix?

[01:57] Lina: mix — small model for autocomplete and a larger one for full rec generation. for POC we'd probably start with a mid-size open model and run a couple of variants. we also care about quantization and whether that skews quality.

[02:15] Priya: under that traffic shape, we'd design a benchmark that replays your diurnal baseline, then injects spike patterns that match the flash-sale bursts. we track token distribution so we can calibrate batching (continuous batching) and KV cache hit-rates for repeated prefixes. for the heavy-tail responses we'll do synthetic long-response tests to exercise memory bandwidth and p99 tails.

[02:42] Carlos: how do you capture the prefix/caching behavior? a lot of our traffic is repeated product-description prompts which should benefit from prefix cache.

[02:51] Priya: good question. we instrument KV cache hit rate in the runtime. during the replay we can toggle cache warmup and show delta on p50/p95/p99 and tokens-per-second. we'll include charts for cache-warm vs cold. typical cache hit improvements for product-repeated prefixes are 2-4x latency reduction on simple prompts.

[03:12] Omar: i want to call out networking again. if we do VPC private option we need to know egress patterns. we cannot allow outbound to public internet from our subnets. can your private offering be fully air-gapped?

[03:27] Priya: Redwood Private can run in a customer VPC with no public egress; we can do an on-prem variant for stricter needs. we'll put that in the runbook. there will be some ops work for whitelisting and IAM integration.

[03:41] Carlos: ok cool. what about autoscaling? during spikes we're worried about cold starts impacting p99.

[03:50] Priya: autoscaling policy will be tuned per-POD with reserved capacity for critical routes. for spikes we'd recommend a mix of reserved burst capacity plus a short warmup window for models that need GPU init. also we can route lower-tier traffic to smaller cheaper variants during spikes as an intentional graceful degradation.

[04:12] Lina: can you run a mixed QPS/concurrency profile? our client uses multiplexed sessions so concurrency distribution matters more than raw QPS. sometimes we have many concurrent small prompts, other times one big prompt.

[04:24] Priya: yes — test harness supports specifying concurrency distributions and inter-arrival times. we can replay real traces or synthesize heavy multiplexed concurrency. we'll capture per-request latency, token throughput, GPU utilization and memory pressure.

[04:41] Jordan: what success metrics should we put into the POC doc? let's propose a candidate set and you tell us if it's realistic.

[04:49] Priya: candidate success criteria: 1) sustained baseline throughput at median QPS with p95 < 180ms 2) spike handling: during 2-3 minute bursts to 1.8k qps p99 < 1.2s with graceful degradation to smaller model for non-critical routes 3) cost delta: less than 20% above your internal cost for same SLA, or identified levers (quantization, caching) that bring it in-range 4) telemetry: per-request tracing and audit logs available in SIEM 5) security: SOC2 attestation and VPC private option signed off.

[05:32] Carlos: those look reasonable, the spike p99 target is acceptable. we'd like the telemetry to include token-level timing and the ability to correlate user IDs (hashed) to latency.

[05:45] Omar: and we need to validate warm/cold start behavior under autoscale and ensure model compilation time doesn't blow up the first request.

[05:54] Priya: acknowledged. we'll include cold-start benchmarks (90/10 traffic splits) and model load times in the report.

[06:03] Lina: on token distribution — i can provide a sample histogram of input/output token percentiles. should we anonymize first?

[06:11] Carlos: yes anonymize. remove any PII. just need token counts, payload shapes, and timing.

[06:18] Jordan: perfect — action item: Lina to export 14 days of anonymized traces (headers, timestamps, prompt length, response length, route) and drop into the secure S3 we provide. we'll give a presigned upload.

[06:31] Lina: noted. will do.

[06:35] Jordan: i'll walk through the timeline. our suggested POC cadence: week 0 (now): scoping + data handoff; week 1: baseline replay with hosted sandbox to establish baseline metrics; week 2: spike testing and cache warmup experiments + model variant runs; week 3: private/VPC setup and end-to-end secure replay if needed; week 4: analysis, optimizations, and sign-off. total ~4 weeks. does that align?

[06:58] Carlos: aligns but we may need 2 extra days for procurement to approve private VPC access.

[07:05] Omar: our security team may request a vulnerability scan of the agent. is that normal?

[07:10] Priya: yes we can coordinate scans and provide SOC2/ISO docs. we usually run a short threat model review with security folks.

[07:18] Lina: one more question: what about model fallback logic — if dedicated capacity is exhausted, how do you prevent errors?

[07:26] Priya: we support policy-based smart routing — fallback to smaller model variants or another region. for hard limits we surface explicit backpressure to the client with healthy retry headers. during the POC we'll exercise fallback policies and measure their effect on latency and quality.

[07:42] Carlos: any gotchas on the cost modeling? We'd like a token-level cost breakdown that includes reserved capacity amortization.

[07:50] Jordan: yes we'll provide cost modeling: per-token runtime cost, reserved capacity amortized across forecasted QPS, and sensitivity to quantization and batching. we'll run a few scenarios: baseline, aggressive caching, and quantized quantile.

[08:05] Omar: can you give an example of the telemetry we get for each request?

[08:10] Priya: per-request: arrival timestamp, model variant, token counts, latency stages (queue, compute, send), GPU ID, KV cache hit boolean, route ID, and an opaque request id you can correlate with your app logs. we can ship to your SIEM or provide a console view.

[08:27] Carlos: good. i want to ensure runbook includes instructions for reproducing a spike and toggling fallback policies.

[08:33] Priya: we'll include reproducible scripts and a runbook section: how to replay, how to change autoscale thresholds, and how to interpret metrics.

[08:40] Jordan: ok let's cover risks and open questions quickly. 1) data residency & on-prem option 2) procurement timeline 3) expected QA resources from AzureGrove for evaluation 4) acceptable error modes during spikes.

[08:56] Carlos: for QA we can assign one engineer full time (Lina) and a part-time SRE. procurement should be a two-week window. error modes: up to 2% request rejection during extreme flash sale is tolerable if documented.

[09:12] Priya: noted. we'll design the POC to expose those rejection rates and fallback impacts.

[09:20] Jordan: any competitors we should watch for?

[09:23] Carlos: Anthropic for generation quality, OpenAI for convenience, and we also benchmark our in-house optimized runtime.

[09:30] Priya: one technical detail — to properly measure heavy-tail responses we recommend running end-to-end latencies with both streaming and non-streaming modes to capture client perceived p99.

[09:41] Omar: okay. one ask: can Redwood provide a short sample of RPC-level logs and the JSON schema so our SIEM ingestion team can validate mappings?

[09:49] Jordan: yes we'll provide a sample log bundle and schema as part of the harness.

[09:54] Carlos: great. seems like we're aligned. i'd like a short written POC scope we can send to procurement.

[09:59] Jordan: we'll produce a one-pager and the full runbook.

[10:03] Priya: recap of deliverables: benchmark harness + scripts, POC test plan, sample log schema, private VPC runbook, anonymized data upload instructions.

[10:12] Lina: + sample token histograms from us.

[10:15] Jordan: next steps and timeline — Jordan to send POC one-pager and presigned S3 for trace upload by Tue 2027-11-23; Lina to upload traces by 2027-11-24; Priya to deliver POC test plan by 2027-11-25. we'll tentatively kick off baseline replay week of 2027-11-29.

[10:36] Carlos: sounds good. thanks everyone.

[10:39] Omar: thanks.

[10:40] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.

[10:45] End meeting.
